The OECD's April 9, 2026 preliminary release put 2025 ODA at USD 174.3 billion. A later OECD report (dated June 2026) revised the projections, so it is the more current source.

- **2025 level:** Total DAC aid came to USD 174.3 billion, or 0.26% of combined GNI, down from USD 215.1 billion in 2024. That is a 23.1% fall compared with 2024 in real terms, which the source calls the steepest drop on record. The June report later revised the 2025 drop to 23.3%.
- **April 2026 projection:** The OECD projected a further 5.8% decline in ODA in 2026, based on a survey of DAC members and published official information.
- **June 2026 projection:** The later report puts 2026 net ODA at about USD 152 billion, a 6.9% fall, which it describes as its lowest level since 2014. It also expects net ODA to be 9.9% lower in 2028 than in 2025, with the ratio slipping to 0.21% of GNI. All figures are in constant 2024 USD. For 2027 and 2028, the projection increasingly assumes flat ODA/GNI at 2025 levels, because fewer donors have published figures.
- **Outside view:** Devpolicy's analysis of the April data calls the OECD's stated-plans outlook more realistically a best case than a central case, based on how far the OECD's June 2025 forecasts overshot. Its own central projection for 33 donors is US$150 billion in 2026, US$139 billion in 2027 and US$136 billion in 2028 in constant 2024 prices.

I did not find a separate 2027 figure from the OECD in these results. The 2026 numbers differ between the April (–5.8%) and June (–6.9%) releases, so check which vintage you need.

input.headline: The biggest difference would be the year-long ceasefire: about 15 state-based conflicts in 2027 instead of about 63, and roughly 16 million fewer displaced people, while the warming projection, the energy investment ratio and the warhead total would barely move.
input.caveat: The baseline depends on whether the Iran and Ukraine wars end in the coming months, and several sources revise past figures by more than one year's change (poverty, hunger, warheads). The with-plan numbers rest on untestable assumptions: how statisticians would book the levy, whether cash worth 11% of GDP keeps its value, and how many ceasefires break in the seven weeks between day 365 and 31 December 2027. I could not open the OECD or SIPRI PDFs, so some trend figures come from secondary coverage.

indicators.unit: million people below $3.00 a day (World Bank)
indicators.resolves: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform: first nowcast for 2027 in the update expected around September 2027 (the September 2026 update carried nowcasts to 2026). Survey-based figures follow from about 2029.
indicators.reasoning: The Bank's September 2026 vintage has 824.3 million in 2024 and its October report 811 million in 2026, with the rate flat since 2019 and the count projected higher by 2030, so I hold it roughly flat; one vintage change alone moved 2024 by 22.5 million. In the plan, cash reaches most of the poorest from April 2027, but it is sized to the old $2.15 line, covers under nine months of 2027 and risks local inflation. I therefore assume only part of the recipients clear $3.00 on a full-year measure.

indicators.unit: million deaths of children under five in the year (UN IGME)
indicators.resolves: UN IGME Levels and Trends in Child Mortality report covering 2027, expected about March 2029 (the March 2026 edition covered 2024).
indicators.reasoning: IGME gave 4.8 million for 2023 and 4.9 million for 2024 with the decline slowed by more than 60% since 2015, and the 2025 aid cuts are not yet in the data, so I expect near-stagnation. The plan adds cash from April 2027, a fully funded humanitarian appeal, ceasefire access, and Gavi and Global Fund money. I assume a fraction of the Kenyan trial effect at scale for part of the year, about 0.25 million fewer deaths, which IGME's smoothed estimates would only partly show.

indicators.unit: million people undernourished (FAO SOFI central estimate)
indicators.resolves: SOFI 2028, expected July 2028 (SOFI 2026 was launched on 21 July 2026 with 2025 data).
indicators.reasoning: Prevalence fell from 8.1% in 2024 to 7.8% in 2025, but the 2026 energy and fertiliser shock from the Iran war and the aid cuts should stall that, and FAO's own 2025 range is 608 to 696 million. In the plan, Hormuz reopens in November 2026, the humanitarian appeal is fully funded, ceasefires open Sudan and Gaza, and cash reaches the poorest for under nine months of 2027. I allow for food price rises in recipient countries cancelling part of the gain.

indicators.unit: million people forcibly displaced at end of year (UNHCR)
indicators.resolves: UNHCR Global Trends report with end-2027 figures, expected June 2028.
